outlooks.summary: Strong to severe thunderstorms are possible from a portion of the Southeast U.S. into the Ohio Valley and southern Great Lakes. Damaging wind and a few tornadoes will be possible along with some hail.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A very strong upper jet will rotate through the base of a potent synoptic upper trough and into the middle MS Valley, Ohio Valley and upper Great Lakes. Surface low within the exit region of this jet will develop northeastward and occlude over WI this afternoon. The trailing cold front will stretch from a surface low in IA early in the day southward through the lower MS Valley. This front will advance east reaching the lower Great Lakes southwest into the middle Gulf coast by the end of this period.

sections.title: Southeast U.S. through Ohio Valley and Great Lakes
sections.text: Initial band of convection developing along warm conveyor belt from the TN Valley into the OH Valley will shift northeast and weaken early Thursday. However, ageostropic forcing accompanying an upstream jet exit region is already spreading through the Southern Plains, contributing to thunderstorms development along the front over northeast TX. This zone of ascent will continue to spread northeast during the early part of the day, and most models develop a secondary band of showers and thunderstorms over the middle MS Valley that shifts into the OH Valley by mid day. The timing and evolution of this early convection and areas of clouds complicate the forecast to some degree. Nevertheless, a corridor of mid-upper 50s dewpoints will advect north into the OH Valley along a strong low-level jet, with mid-upper 60s farther south across the Southeast States. MLCAPE should range from 1000+ J/kg over the Southeast States, where more diabatic heating is possible and higher dewpoints will reside, to around 500 J/kg farther north into the OH Valley and southern Great Lakes. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are likely from portions of the Southeast U.S. into the Ohio Valley and southern Great Lakes. Damaging winds and a few tornadoes will be possible along with large hail.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: An upper-level low over Iowa this morning will gradually evolve into an open wave as it lifts northeast across the Great Lakes today, while a trailing portion of the trough extends southwest into the central Plains. A deep (983 mb) surface low beneath the upper low will lift northeast as a trailing cold front moves rapidly across the TN/OH Valley region and the lower MS Valley. Collectively, these surface and upper-level features will result in a broad area of favorable vertical wind shear for severe storms.

sections.title: Southeast U.S. through Ohio Valley and Great Lakes
sections.text: An expansive area of showers and thunderstorms associated with warm/moist advection within the warm sector was in progress at 13Z, and the effects of ongoing/early day precipitation casts some uncertainty on the details regarding severe potential today and tonight. In general, ongoing precipitation should weaken or lift northeast of the risk area by midday, with additional thunderstorm development in advance of the cold front by afternoon. Low-level moisture remains a limiting factor, with lower/mid 50s surface dew points expected as far north as OH/southeast Lower Michigan, and mid 60s/upper across the southeast states. Substantial cloud cover combined with modest mid-level lapse rates will temper instability, with MLCAPE ranging from 1000+ J/kg over the Southeast States, where more diabatic heating is possible and higher dewpoints will reside, to around 300-500 J/kg farther north into the OH Valley and southern Great Lakes. The impressive low/mid-level wind fields will result in deep-layer shear averaging 50 kts across the southeast to in excess of 80 kts across the OH Valley/Great Lakes, with low-level (0-1 km) SRH in excess of 300 m2/s2. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are likely from portions of the Southeast U.S. into the Ohio Valley and southern Great Lakes. Several tornadoes, a few of which could be strong, damaging winds and isolated large hail will be possible through this evening.

sections.title: TN Valley to the OH Valley through this evening
sections.text: A deep surface cyclone in southeastern NE will move northeastward over IA/WI/upper MI by this evening, as an associated mid-upper jet streak ejects northeastward from MO toward the lower Great Lakes. A surface cold front will progress eastward from the mid MS Valley to the OH Valley, and southeastward into the lower MS Valley. A narrow corridor of low-level moistening and some surface heating in cloud breaks is expected immediately ahead of the cold front through this afternoon, which will support some destabilization as far northeast southern Lower MI. The strongest low-level flow will develop northeastward across TN toward OH through the afternoon. Vertical shear will be very strong within the warm sector, with effective bulk shear of 70-80 kt and effective SRH of 400-600 m2/s2. Boundary-layer dewpoints in the low 60s have spread as far north as the lower OH River as of late morning, and some additional moistening is expected to the northeast through the afternoon. Midlevel lapse rates are not particularly steep and surface heating will be slowed by the morning convection/clouds, so MLCAPE will likely remain in the 500-1000 J/kg range. Wind profiles will clearly favor supercells,

sections.title: Central/northeastern IL to southern Lower MI this afternoon
sections.text: Bands of convection are developing along the nose of the primary frontal surge/dry slot near and north of Saint Louis as of mid morning. The low levels are destabilizing northward across IL with surface heating in cloud breaks and boundary-layer dewpoints of 56-60 expected to reach northeastern IL by early afternoon. A broken band of low-topped thunderstorms is expected along the wind shift by this afternoon, when strong vertical shear will support supercells capable of producing tornadoes, damaging gusts, and marginally severe hail. The convection will subsequently spread northeastward toward lower MI later this afternoon. The degree of destabilization is more questionable compared to areas farther southwest, but wind profiles will strongly favor organized/supercell storms. ..Thompson/Bentley.. 03/14/2019

sections.title: 20z Update
sections.text: Large-scale evolution of ongoing convective regime suggests three primary corridors of organized thunderstorm activity will be noted into the evening hours. 20z update will be predicated on these scenarios: 1. MS-TN: Strongest buoyancy currently extends across the central Gulf States into portions of northern AL. Over the last few hours numerous supercells have evolved along a SW-NE oriented corridor along southern fringe of strong mid-high level flow. High-res model guidance supports this orientation/location of supercell activity. Given radar trends will separate the ENH Risk region to more accurately reflect this threat. 2. IN-OH: Early-morning supercells that developed along the OH River across western KY into southern IN continue in a SW-NE oriented fashion, but have shifted downstream in line with aforementioned high-res model guidance. While 14/19z ILN sounding does not exhibit more than weak instability, strongly sheared, surface-based instability has developed ahead of this activity. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat of damaging wind gusts and tornadoes will persist across Tornado Watch 23 for at least the next two hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms within Tornado Watch 23 have struggled to maintain organization and intensity over the past two hours. Storms have had an elongated downshear structure, indicative of storms developing within a weakly unstable but strongly sheared air mass. Warmer temperatures and slightly better moisture downstream results in an air mass that is slightly more thermodynamically supportive of deep convection. Very strong flow aloft continues, with vertical shear more than supportive of organized storms. Consequently, the potential for organized storms capable of damaging wind gusts and tornadoes is expected to persist across Tornado Watch 23 for at least the next two hours. ..Mosier.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Supercell intensity via strengthening low-level mesocyclones will probably intensify further during the next few hours as heating and a slight increase in buoyancy contribute to a greater tornado risk spreading northeast in a destabilizing warm sector.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows broken cloud cover across the lower OH Valley with a couple of supercells moving quickly northeast (230 deg at 52kt). Surface analysis shows temperatures over western KY ranging from near 70 degrees F with surface dewpoints in the lower 60s. Farther northeast in southwest IN and adjacent portions to the east along the OH River, temperatures are rising into the upper 50s to near 60 with dewpoints in the upper 50s. The PAH VAD shows 500 m2/s2 0-1km SRH. 13Z RAP forecast soundings indicate as the airmass gradually destabilizes during the late morning, a risk for low-level mesocyclones capable of a tornado threat will likely increase. Upwards of 500 J/kg MLCAPE is expected to develop. Currently thinking the greatest risk for tornadoes will accompany the quasi-discrete supercell activity as it moves from western KY downstream into southwest IN during the next several hours which will coincide with the diurnal heating cycle on the north-end of the near 60 degrees F surface dewpoints.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Tornado watch 23 will be allowed to expire at 17Z. A downstream watch is not likely in the near term.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection has weakened across tornado watch 23 with little if any lightning remaining. No additional storm intensification is expected in the next few hours. Therefore, the tornado watch will be allowed to expire at 17Z with no downstream watch likely in the near term. An additional tornado watch may be needed by later this afternoon in at least portions of this area as low-level moisture advection and heating through breaks in the clouds leads to some destabilization. ..Bentley.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will continue to intensify over the next 1-2 hours and likely become surface-based across central IL. A tornado risk will probably accompany the stronger storms with the tornado risk perhaps moving into northeast IL early this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery shows mostly clear skies across central IL with breaks in the clouds over northeast IL into northwest IN as of 1030am CDT. A mid-level vorticity maximum located over the mid MS Valley is expected to move northeast across central IL during the next several hours. Surface analysis shows temperatures warming into the lower 60s with dewpoints rising into the upper 50s over central IL. The 12Z Lincoln, IL raob showed a very cold 500mb temperature (-21.7 deg C) with an 8 degree C/km 700-500mb lapse rate, it appears 750-1000 J/kg MLCAPE is possible. Given the very strong to extreme shear profile coupled with the very steep lapse rate, it appears tornado potential is greater than previously anticipated and an upgrade in tornado probabilities will be reflected in the upcoming 1630Z convective outlook. If robust surface-based supercells in fact develop, a strong tornado is possible mainly east of the US51/I-39 corridor in east-central and into northeast portions of IL this afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A gradual increase in storms is expected through the afternoon. A tornado watch will likely be needed soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 16Z surface analysis shows much of northeast Mississippi and northwest Alabama has warmed 4 to 5 F in the last hour despite some cloud cover across the area. This has led to an increase in low-level instability to around 750 to 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE. Warming is expected to continue with low-level moisture advection which will lead to moderate instability by mid-afternoon. The recent heating in this area has provided enough instability for a reinvigoration of lightning from some of the convection in northern Mississippi. Therefore, expect more widespread storm coverage within the next hour or two as surface destabilization continues to increase. Deep-layer shear in this area is very favorable for supercell and low-level mesocyclone development with deep layer effective shear around 55 to 60 knots and 0-1 SRH around 350 m2/s2 per GWX VWP. Therefore, these storms will pose a tornado threat with the potential for strong tornadoes, especially as supercells mature into northwest Alabama.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Supercell tornado potential appears greatest near the OH River in the vicinity of Owensboro during the next hour and shifting eastward with time. Surface pressure falls are greatest in the Kentuckiana region which is at north edge of richer low-level moisture.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface analysis indicates an area of pressure falls (3-4mb per 2 hours) is located from near Owensboro, east to Louisville, and north to Columbus, IN. A southwest-northeast band of quasi-discrete supercells will move into this region from the west. Richer low-level moisture is concentrated from I-64 and south as evident by surface observations with dewpoints near 60 degrees F in the vicinity of I-64 to 63F at Owensboro as of 12pm CDT/1pm EDT. RAP forecast soundings also imply the greatest tornado risk in this small corridor where buoyancy (500 J/kg MLCAPE) and 0-1km SRH (400 m2/s2) are juxtaposed during the next 1-2 hours. Farther north into south-central IN, more marginal moisture will tend to limit an otherwise greater risk for tornadoes. ..Smith.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Several supercells have developed between Jackson and Columbus, MS. These supercells are expected to strengthen through the afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several supercells have started to exhibit moderate mid-level rotation between Jackson and Columbus, MS. Low-level rotation in the appendages of these supercells have been noticeably absent for the past hour. This is likely due to lower instability farther north (500 to 750 J/kg MLCAPE near Columbus) and lower low-level shear farther south (125 m2/s2 0-1 SRH at DGX VWP). Through the afternoon, instability is expected to increase to 1000 to 1500 J/kg ahead of these storms as they move east into an environment with over 300 m2/s2 0-1 SRH via GWX VWP. As the tornadic environment becomes more favorable through the afternoon, expect low-level rotation to start to organize with an increasing tornado threat. ..Bentley.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few damaging gusts are possible this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a band of quasi-discrete storms over northeast IL moving into The Region in northwest IN. Surface temperatures early this afternoon have remained relatively tempered in the lower 60s in IN to the middle-upper 50s over southwest Lower MI. A strong wind profile will support storm organization with the most organized storm structures capable of strong to locally severe gusts. Tornado potential will likely be limited especially as the northern IL activity moves away from a moist axis near the IN/IL border.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated supercells are possible with large hail and damaging winds as the primary threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface-based storm development has started across southern Mississippi along and ahead of a surface front currently from near Jackson, MS to far southwest MS. Cross boundary effective shear around 40 to 45 knots and MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg should support discrete supercell development. Weaker lower tropospheric flow and somewhat veered surface winds have led to relatively weaker low-level shear in this area. While tornadoes cannot be ruled out, the tornado threat is much lower in southern Mississippi than in Tornado Watch 25. Limited storm coverage will likely preclude the need for a watch in this area, but if supercell coverage becomes more scattered, a watch may be needed.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Several supercells have developed within tornado watch 25. The highest tornado threat will be over north central Alabama for the next several hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A line of supercells has continued into northern Alabama. These storms have exhibited good mid-level rotation, but low-level rotation has been limited. The 18Z Birmingham sounding showed a small inversion between 850mb and 700mb which has likely limited more robust updraft development up to this point. Farther north, the 18Z Huntsville Vortex-SE sounding showed limited instability. Given extensive cloud cover which has now overspread this area and northward moisture transport which is becoming increasingly cut off with northward extent, expect the severe threat has decreased significantly in the northern half of tornado watch 25. This is further supported by the 18Z HRRR which shows convection intensity decreasing across far northern Alabama and central Tennessee. The best region for a continued severe and tornado threat will likely be from areas south and east of Columbus, MS to areas near Tuscaloosa and north of Birmingham over the next 2 hours. In this area, instability has increased with MLCAPE in excess of 1000 J/kg and low-level shear remains moderate to strong (>250 m2/s2 0-1 SRH according to 18Z BMX sounding and 19Z BMX VWP). In addition, the storms in Kemper County, MS and Lamar County, AL have shown considerable updraft strengthening in the last 30 minutes suggesting that this region is starting to feel the effects of better buoyancy. ..Bentley.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Ongoing broken line of thunderstorms should continue to pose an isolated large hail and damaging wind threat for the next couple of hours. Watch issuance is possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong large-scale forcing for ascent preceding an upper trough/low has encouraged scatted thunderstorm development this afternoon across parts of southern Lower MI. Some clearing has allowed temperatures to warm into the mid 50s to mid 60s ahead of this ongoing convection. Even though low-level moisture remains limited, the modest heating coupled with some steepening of mid-level lapse rates is supporting MLCAPE of 250-500 J/kg across parts of southern Lower MI. Strong effective bulk shear of 50-75+ kt will support organized updrafts, and isolated instances of large hail and damaging winds should continue to be possible as these thunderstorms move eastward over the next couple of hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Vigorous thunderstorm development, including a few supercells, will likely continue, with a slow eastward progression across mainly central and eastern Alabama, through 8-10 PM EDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Discrete thunderstorm development, including supercells, continues, and appears generally focused along a confluent zone near a lingering 40+ kt south/southwesterly 850 mb jet axis. The jet appears likely to undergo only a gradually weakening into early evening, in the wake of the deep cyclone migrating across the Great Lakes, with also only a relatively slow eastward progression. Given the corridor of weak to moderate boundary layer instability along this axis, supported by mid 60s surface dew points, the environment appears likely to remain supportive of supercells with potential for tornadoes into at least the 00-02Z time frame. It is possible that some of this activity could spread into portions of northwestern Georgia, but activity seems likely to remain to the west of the Atlanta metropolitan area, where a more stable environment is expected to generally prevail. ..Kerr.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Mainly a damaging wind threat continues across southern portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 27. Isolated large hail also remains possible, and a tornado cannot be ruled out.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Broken line of supercells and small bowing clusters continues across parts of northern/central KY into southwestern OH at 23Z. This convection has produced strong to damaging winds and several reports of 1.00-1.75 inch diameter hail over the past couple of hours. The best short term severe threat appears to be confined to mainly southern portions of WW 27 where slightly greater low-level moisture and weak instability is present. Regardless, 50-65 kt of effective bulk shear will continue to organize updrafts, and damaging winds will probably be the main threat into this evening as storm interactions occur and convection potentially grows upscale into a broken line. A brief tornado cannot be completely ruled out, especially across northern KY where thunderstorms are a bit more discrete and effective SRH is maximized. ..Gleason.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat should be maximized over a small part of southern Lower MI over the next hour or so. A strong to damaging wind and isolated tornado threat continues.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Although thunderstorms have remained low-topped across southern Lower MI over the past hour, at least one TDS has been observed with a rotational velocity couplet in Shiawassee County. MLCAPE remains weak, generally in the 250-500 J/kg range, but this is apparently sufficient to support surface-based thunderstorms with both a damaging wind an isolated tornado threat. A strongly veering wind profile in the 0-1 km layer per KDTX VWP is supporting updraft rotation, with effective SRH of 350-400+ m2/s2 estimated from 23Z mesoanalysis. Another low-topped supercell has developed ahead of the broken line of thunderstorms, and given the degree of low-level shear, an isolated tornado could occur in the next hour or so. Beyond 01Z (9 pm EDT), instability should weaken further, and the overall severe threat should gradually diminish. ..Gleason.. 03/14/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe threat will continue across eastern portions of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 27 for the next hour or so. Downstream watch issuance into more of eastern OH is unlikely at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A 75-100+ kt southwesterly mid-level jet is beginning to overspread northern KY and OH this evening. A very strong 50-65+ kt south-southwesterly low-level jet is also shifting eastward across the same region. Strongly veering winds through mid levels associated with both jets are resulting in 50-75+ kt of effective bulk shear. Organized, rotating updrafts have been detected on radar within the ongoing small clusters and bowing line segments across OH into northern KY. Mainly wind damage and occasional severe wind gusts have been reported over the past hour or two given the largely linear mode and steepened low-level lapse rates from diurnal heating. These thunderstorms are beginning to outpace the low-level moisture return, especially across eastern OH where surface dewpoints generally remain in the upper 40s to around 50. Current expectations are for the ongoing isolated severe threat to continue for another hour or so before gradually diminishing due to the lack of sufficient instability to support surface-based thunderstorms. Therefore, downstream watch issuance into eastern OH appears unlikely at this time. ..Gleason.. 03/15/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Primarily an isolated strong to damaging wind threat should continue across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 28 through 02Z (10 pm EDT).
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar imagery shows thunderstorms have congealed into a line across southeastern Lower MI. Modifying the 00Z DTX sounding for current observations across this region shows weak but sufficient instability to support surface-based thunderstorm potential for about the next hour. Effective bulk shear around 60-70 kt will continue to organize these thunderstorms. Isolated strong to damaging winds should remain the main threat given the linear nature of the convection. With a current east-northeastward motion storm motion of 40-50 kt, these thunderstorms should move east of WW 28 around 02Z, which is the scheduled expiration time. ..Gleason.. 03/15/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A couple of severe storms linger across parts of central through east central Alabama, but severe weather potential, in general, is in the process of diminishing. If trends continue as currently anticipated through the next hour or two, it is possible that the remaining valid portions of the watch could be cancelled prior to the scheduled Midnight CDT (1 AM EDT) expiration.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Considerable general weakening of discrete pre-frontal thunderstorm activity has been evident for the past hour or so in radar and lightning data. A south-southwesterly 850 mb jet axis lingers as far south as northwestern Georgia into central Alabama, but wind speeds are gradually weakening, and a relatively moist unstable boundary layer along it is gradually becoming less unstable with the loss of daytime heating. There has been some increase in convection to the northwest and west of the region, across the Cumberland Plateau into the lower Mississippi Valley, just ahead of where a corridor of weak to moderate boundary layer instability appears to linger near a remnant dry line. However, potential for substantive further intensification of this activity seems limited, in the presence of neutral to rising mid-level heights in the wake of the cyclone over the Great Lakes region, before the trailing cold front overtakes the dry line/instability axis later this evening. ..Kerr.. 03/15/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
